title: Non-Markovian heavy-quark equilibration and equilibrium correlation function in a thermal medium
authors: Monisha Nair, Juan Torres-Rincon, Santosh K. Das
abstract: We compute the charm-quark current-current correlation function within the Langevin framework and extract the heavy-quark diffusion coefficient using the Green--Kubo formula. The formalism is further extended to evaluate the correlation function using a generalized Langevin equation that incorporates memory effects via an exponentially decaying memory kernel. We find that while memory effects qualitatively modify the transient structure of the current correlations, the value of the transport coefficient remains unchanged in the non-relativistic limit. In addition, we investigate heavy-quark thermalization in the presence of memory and compare the non-equilibrium solution of a generalized Fokker--Planck equation with the one obtained from the generalized Langevin equation in the non-relativistic limit. We also consider the relativistic version of the correlated noise case and observe that memory effects can give rise to a damped, oscillatory equilibration of the heavy quark in a non-Markovian bath.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how heavy quarks thermalize and diffuse in a hot medium by extending standard Langevin descriptions to include memory effects. It calculates transport coefficients like the diffusion coefficient using correlation functions derived from generalized Fokker-Planck equations. The findings show that while memory introduces oscillatory behavior, it maintains consistency with established results in certain limits.
main_problem: The study investigates heavy-quark (HQ) equilibration and correlation functions within a thermal medium, specifically focusing on incorporating non-Markovian memory effects.
main_result: Memory effects qualitatively alter the transient structure of current correlations but do not change the transport coefficient in the non-relativistic limit; however, they can induce damped, oscillatory equilibration in the relativistic case.
method: The analysis employs kinetic theory approaches, utilizing generalized Langevin equations and comparing solutions derived from both the generalized Fokker-Planck equation and the corresponding Langevin framework.
model_or_system: The system models heavy quarks (charm/beauty) propagating through a hot, dense medium like the Quark-Gluon Plasma. The dynamics are governed by stochastic processes incorporating memory kernels into the standard Markovian description.
key_observables: Heavy-quark diffusion coefficient ($D_s$), HQ momentum distribution function $f(\mathbf{p}, t)$, and current–current correlation functions $\langle \mathbf{j}(t) \cdot \mathbf{j}(0) angle$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), heavy quark mass ($m$), drag coefficient ($A$), and memory time ($	au_m$). The analysis compares non-relativistic (NR) and relativistic limits.
main_assumptions: The work assumes space homogeneity, uses the Green-Kubo formula to relate transport coefficients to equilibrium correlations, and often relies on approximations like constant drag coefficients or assumed exponential decay forms for correlation functions at large times.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of $D_s(t^*)$ calculated via integrating the current-current correlation function $C(t)$, showing plateaus that approach an asymptotic value, which is sensitive to the chosen integration cutoff time $t^*$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the foundational Langevin/Fokker-Planck framework (Markovian case), extending it to include memory effects via generalized equations, calculating key observables like $D_s$ using Green-Kubo relations in both NR and relativistic limits, and finally comparing numerical solutions across different time regimes.
why_interesting: The incorporation of non-Markovian dynamics is crucial for accurately modeling relaxation processes in strongly coupled systems where memory effects cannot be ignored, providing a more realistic description than simple white noise approximations.
